scenarios.title: Price Negotiation
scenarios.desc: A buyer wants a lower price. Practice your negotiation skills.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: Hi, I'm interested in your LED night light. But the price of $2.50 is too high. Can you give me a better price?

options.text: Yes, I can give you 20% off right now.
options.feedback: Too easy! Never give a big discount immediately. The buyer will think your original price was inflated. Try to understand their needs first.

options.text: I understand. How many units are you looking to order? We offer tiered pricing based on quantity.
options.feedback: Great! Asking about quantity first is the right move. It helps you understand their needs and gives you room to negotiate.

options.text: Sorry, our prices are fixed. We cannot offer any discount.
options.feedback: Too rigid! Even if you can't discount much, you should explore other options like volume pricing or bundling. This response may lose the customer.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: I need about 500 units. But my budget is around $2.00 per unit. Can you do that?

options.text: $2.00 is below our cost. But for 500 units, I can offer $2.30. That's already our best price.
options.feedback: Good! You explained why you can't meet the price and made a reasonable counter-offer. Always justify your price.

options.text: OK, $2.00 is fine.
options.feedback: Too quick to agree! If you accept immediately, the buyer will wonder if they could have gotten even lower. Always negotiate.

options.text: No way. The price is $2.50, take it or leave it.
options.feedback: Too aggressive! This will likely end the conversation. Try to find a middle ground.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: $2.30 is still a bit high. What if I increase the order to 1000 units? Can you do $2.10?

options.text: For 1000 units, I can do $2.15. And I can include free shipping to your warehouse. That's our best offer.
options.feedback: Excellent! You acknowledged the larger order, made a small concession, and added value with free shipping. This is how you close a deal.

options.text: OK, $2.10 for 1000 units. Deal!
options.feedback: You gave in too easily. You could have gotten a better margin. Always add value (shipping, packaging, etc.) instead of just dropping price.

options.text: 1000 units at $2.10? That's impossible. Our cost is already $2.05.
options.feedback: Never reveal your cost! This gives the buyer too much information. Also, if your margin is only $0.05, you need to reconsider your pricing strategy.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: OK, $2.15 with free shipping sounds fair. Let's do it!

options.text: Great! I will send you the Proforma Invoice today. Please confirm the shipping address and arrange the deposit.
options.feedback: Perfect! You closed the deal professionally. Always follow up with documentation promptly.

options.text: Awesome! By the way, we also have other products you might like.
options.feedback: Good attempt at cross-selling, but make sure to close this deal first before introducing new products. Send the PI first!

scenarios.title: Customer Complaint
scenarios.desc: A customer is angry about a defective product. Handle it professionally.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: I received my order yesterday and 3 out of 10 phone cases are scratched! This is unacceptable. I want a full refund!

options.text: I'm sorry to hear that. But are you sure it was our fault? It could be the shipping company.
options.feedback: Never blame others or question the customer first! This makes them more angry. Always apologize first and take responsibility.

options.text: I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. Could you please send us photos of the damaged items so we can investigate and resolve this quickly?
options.feedback: Perfect! You apologized sincerely and asked for evidence professionally. This shows you care and want to solve the problem.

options.text: OK, we will give you a full refund right away.
options.feedback: Too quick! You should investigate first. Some complaints may be exaggerated or fraudulent. Always ask for photos/evidence before committing to a refund.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: Fine, here are the photos. You can see the scratches clearly. What are you going to do about it?

options.text: Thank you for the photos. We will send 3 replacement cases today via express shipping at no cost. You don't need to return the damaged ones. Is that OK?
options.feedback: Excellent! You offered a clear solution quickly, didn't ask for returns (which costs more in shipping), and used express shipping to show urgency.

options.text: We can refund you $3 for the 3 damaged cases.
options.feedback: A small refund might not satisfy an angry customer. Replacements + keeping the damaged items is usually better for customer satisfaction.

options.text: Please return all 10 cases to us and we will send you a full refund.
options.feedback: Bad idea! Making the customer return everything is inconvenient and will make them more frustrated. Offer a partial solution instead.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: OK, that sounds reasonable. But I'm still not happy about this. What if it happens again?

options.text: I completely understand your frustration. We have reported this to our quality control team and will add extra protective packaging for your future orders. As a gesture of goodwill, here is a 10% discount code for your next purchase.
options.feedback: Perfect! You acknowledged their feelings, explained preventive measures, and offered compensation. This turns a negative experience into a positive one.

options.text: It won't happen again. Our products are usually perfect.
options.feedback: Avoid dismissive language. The customer experienced a real problem. Acknowledge it and explain what you're doing to prevent it.

scenarios.title: Shipping Delay
scenarios.desc: A customer's order is delayed. Manage expectations professionally.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: It's been 2 weeks and my order still hasn't arrived! The tracking hasn't updated in 5 days. Where is my package?!

options.text: Let me check with the logistics company and get back to you.
options.feedback: OK but too vague. The customer wants immediate reassurance. Set a specific timeline for when you'll get back to them.

options.text: I apologize for the delay. I will contact the shipping company immediately and give you an update within 24 hours. Rest assured, we will track this until it's delivered.
options.feedback: Excellent! You apologized, committed to action, set a clear timeline (24h), and reassured the customer.

options.text: Shipping delays are normal. Please be patient.
options.feedback: Never dismiss a customer's concern! 'Be patient' is the worst thing you can say. Always show you're taking action.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: OK, please check and let me know. This is for a customer of mine and I'm losing business.

options.text: I understand this is urgent. I checked with the carrier and your package is held at customs. I'm expediting the clearance process. New ETA is 3-5 days. I'll also offer you free shipping on your next order for the inconvenience.
options.feedback: Perfect! You investigated, found the root cause, took action, provided a new ETA, and offered compensation. This is professional crisis management.

options.text: It's stuck at customs. There's nothing I can do, you just have to wait.
options.feedback: Never say 'nothing I can do'! Even if it's customs, you can contact your logistics partner to expedite, or offer alternatives. Always show you're trying.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: Alright, thanks for checking. I hope it arrives soon.

options.text: You're welcome. I will personally monitor this shipment and update you daily until it's delivered. Thank you for your patience.
options.feedback: Perfect closing! Personal commitment + daily updates shows exceptional service. This customer will trust you again.

options.text: No problem. Let me know if you need anything else.
options.feedback: Too passive. Show initiative by offering to monitor the shipment and provide updates. Go the extra mile.

scenarios.title: Cold Outreach
scenarios.desc: Reach out to a potential customer for the first time.

steps.speaker: you
steps.text: (You need to write a cold outreach message to a potential buyer)

options.text: Hi, we are a manufacturer of phone accessories. We can offer you the best prices. Please check our catalog.
options.feedback: Too generic! 'Best prices' is what everyone says. You need a hook - something specific that solves their problem.

options.text: Hi John, I noticed your store sells phone cases on Shopee. We manufacture premium silicone cases that are trending in Southeast Asia. Our MOQ is just 100 units and we can deliver to your PH warehouse in 7 days. Would you like a free sample?
options.feedback: Excellent! You personalized the message, mentioned their platform, highlighted a trending product, low MOQ, fast delivery, and offered a free sample. This gets responses.

options.text: Dear Sir/Madam, We are pleased to introduce our company...
options.feedback: Too formal and generic! 'Dear Sir/Madam' shows you didn't research them. Use their name and show you know their business.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: Thanks for reaching out. The silicone cases sound interesting. But I already have a supplier. Why should I switch?

options.text: Our prices are cheaper than your current supplier.
options.feedback: Price alone is not a strong enough reason to switch. Buyers care about quality, reliability, and service too. Highlight your unique value.

options.text: I understand you have a reliable supplier. We're not asking you to switch immediately. How about trying our free sample first? You can compare the quality yourself. No commitment needed. We also offer OEM customization if you want your own brand.
options.feedback: Perfect! You acknowledged their situation, removed pressure (no commitment), offered a risk-free trial, and mentioned OEM as a differentiator. This is how you get a foot in the door.

options.text: Our quality is much better than other suppliers.
options.feedback: Claiming 'better quality' without proof is empty. Offer samples or data to back up your claim.

steps.speaker: buyer
steps.text: OK, I'll try the sample. Where should I start?

options.text: Great! Please share your shipping address and I'll send the sample today. I'll also include our latest catalog and price list. Once you receive it, I'll follow up to get your feedback.
options.feedback: Perfect! You're taking immediate action, providing additional value (catalog), and setting up a follow-up. This is professional sales execution.

options.text: Sure, just visit our website and place an order.
options.feedback: Too hands-off! For a sample, you should handle everything personally. Don't make the buyer do the work.

scenarios.title: Order Confirmation
scenarios.desc: Confirm an order with a customer after they agree to buy.

steps.speaker: you
steps.text: (The customer agreed to order 500 LED lights at $2.30 each. Now confirm the order details.)

options.text: Great, thanks! I'll process your order now.
options.feedback: Too vague! Always confirm order details in writing to avoid misunderstandings. Include product, qty, price, total, payment terms, and delivery time.

options.text:
Thank you for your order! Please confirm the details below:

Product: LED Night Light (White)
Quantity: 500 units
Unit Price: $2.30
Total: $1,150
Payment: 30% deposit ($345) + 70% balance before shipment
Lead Time: 15 days after deposit
Shipping: FOB Shenzhen

Please confirm and I'll send the Proforma Invoice.
options.feedback: Excellent! You listed all details clearly. This prevents disputes and shows professionalism. Always put everything in writing.

options.text: OK, send me the money and I'll ship it.
options.feedback: Way too casual and unprofessional! You need to provide full order details and a formal PI before requesting payment.

steps.speaker: customer
steps.text: Confirmed! Please send the PI. When do I need to pay the deposit?

options.text: I'll send the PI within 1 hour. The deposit is due within 3 days. Once received, we start production immediately. I'll send you production photos when it starts.
options.feedback: Perfect! Clear timeline, immediate action, and proactive updates. This builds trust and confidence.

options.text: Whenever you're ready to pay is fine.
options.feedback: Too casual! Set a clear deadline for the deposit so production can start on time. Vague timelines lead to delays.
